prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, using bifunctional degraders and molecular glues to direct the ubiquitin-proteasome system to chosen proteins

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation has a clear underlying principle (chemically induced proximity between a target and an E3 ligase), a distinct new capability (removing a protein rather than inhibiting it, which reaches targets once thought undruggable), and large generative potential, which is what I look for after the 2024 and 2025 prizes. Opening support is the broadest on the table: three first-place rankings and a top-four placement from eight of eight members, so it is robust across very different fields, not just a chemical-biology constituency. Crews and Deshaies supply the PROTAC concept and first demonstrations; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains molecular glues mechanistically and gives the story a second, independently grounded pillar. Naming the principle rather than the modality lets the citation be explained to a broad audience.
statement.case_against: I put this fourth in my opening ballot and the reservation has not gone away: clinical validation is incomplete, with PROTACs in late-stage trials but, as far as I can tell, none approved, and the biophysics of ternary-complex cooperativity is only partly quantified. Credit is also crowded (Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito, Kim all have real claims) and a three-person cap forces an arbitrary line between the PROTAC and molecular-glue strands. Nanopore sequencing (B002) is the more mature technology and has a cleaner physical principle, so a reasonable chair could still prefer it.

responses.point: Aili ranks B019 first and argues that Crews, Deshaies and Handa together cover the concept, the first demonstrations and the cereblon mechanism behind glue degraders.
responses.response: I now agree with that trio over my own opening trio, which replaced Handa with Ciulli. Handa's cereblon work is a separate discovery that gives the field its mechanistic unification, and it ties glues and PROTACs to one principle. I still want the committee to say explicitly what Ciulli's VHL ligand and structural work added, because it is the strongest case for displacing someone. Aili's own uncertainty about unverified approval status is shared by me and should be settled before final ballots.

responses.point: Aqvist ranks B019 first, calls induced proximity a new drug modality that is conceptually simple and already a game-changer, and anchors on the PROTAC strand with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli.
responses.response: I agree on the concept. Where I differ is on Ciulli versus Handa: Aqvist treats the molecular-glue arm as a competing credit stream, but I think it is the same principle viewed from the other side, and it is the part with an approved drug lineage (the IMiDs) and a clear mechanism. Dropping it makes the citation narrower than the field. If the group wants a PROTAC-only citation, Ciulli is the right third name, but I would argue that is the less complete story.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling (B034) first as a general reaction used throughout pharmaceutical synthesis, and notes that B019 may be premature because no PROTAC is approved.
responses.response: The premature point is fair and is my own main reservation. But I would separate the two cases: Buchwald-Hartwig amination is a profound and mature extension of palladium cross-coupling, whose core was recognised in 2010, while degradation opens a new modality. The ligand-design story is excellent, yet I would ask whether it is a refinement of the recognised principle rather than a new one. I do not dismiss B034 and would keep it in contention for a later year, but I do not think it displaces B019 this year.

responses.point: Sparr ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B045) first for the physical chemistry of lipid-nucleic acid assembly and for their global clinical validation, while noting the credit is crowded.
responses.response: I take the physical-chemistry argument seriously: pKa tuning and microfluidic assembly are real principles, and the societal impact is undeniable. My hesitation is attribution and overlap, since the delivery technology was only partly invented in one lab and the 2023 Medicine prize already recognised the mRNA side. I would want to hear from Sparr what single discovery the citation names. At present I find the degradation case easier to state in one sentence.

responses.point: Zou ranks ordered mesoporous silica (B005) first as an original, structurally well-characterized materials discovery that is mature and arguably overdue.
responses.response: I agree it is original and mature, and that maturity is a strength. My concern is generative reach: I would like to know whether mesoporous silica opened a new capability comparable to degraders or nanopores, or whether its main legacy is as a supports-and-templates platform. Zou is better placed to judge, and I am open to being persuaded, but the credit dispute between Mobil, FSM-16 and SBA lines also needs a clear answer before I could support it.

uncertainties: Whether any PROTAC has received regulatory approval, which would settle my maturity concern.
Whether the third name should be Handa (molecular glue strand) or Ciulli (PROTAC design and structural work).
Whether a PROTAC plus glue citation is one discovery or two, and whether a two-part prize would be cleaner.
How to weigh nanopore sequencing's maturity and physical clarity against the broader support for B019.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I am a physicist at Lund and share an institution with committee members Somfai and Sparr, but none of the shortlisted candidates is identified in my profile as a colleague, collaborator or Lund affiliate.
